scenario.figure_or_table: Fig. 9 (MLTD within 1 mm radius for single-threaded gobmk after idle warmup), with Table I, Table II and Fig. 5
scenario.description: Transient perf-power-therm co-simulation of a 7nm Skylake-like 7-core client CPU running single-threaded gobmk on one core at a time after an idle thermal warm-up. Maximum localized temperature difference (MLTD) is computed within a 1 mm radius. The 7nm MLTD peaks at almost 70 C versus under 60 C for 14nm, and is highest for cores 0, 2 and 5. The paper packet gives no per-block x, y, width, height or power values, only Table I areas and the Fig. 5 floorplan image, so no floorplan can be extracted from the text.
scenario.architecture: 7nm out-of-order Skylake-like client CPU, 7 cores with 2-way SMT, about 1.25 mm2 per core (about 5 mm2 die at 14nm scaled 50% per node), 224-entry ROB, private L1 and L2, shared L3; 3D-ICE v3.0.0 stack of silicon, solder TIM, copper heat spreader, thermal grease and heatsink
scenario.workload: SPEC2006 gobmk, single-threaded, run on each core individually; 200M-instruction region of interest after cache warm-up, 1M-cycle time step
scenario.operating_point: 1.4 V and 5 GHz (turbo), idle-warmup initial thermal state, 7nm node; hotspot thresholds Tth=80 C, MLTDth=25 C, radius 1 mm; 40 C local ambient assumed for TDP

original_setup.solver: 3D-ICE v3.0.0 compact transient thermal model (CTTM), driven by Sniper (instruction-window-centric/ROB model) performance simulation and a modified McPAT v1.2 power model (extended to 14/10/7nm). Stack: silicon (active layer plus bulk), solder TIM, copper heat spreader, thermal grease, HS483-ND heatsink with P14752-ND fan at 6000 rpm (pdf pages 3-4, Table II).
original_setup.optimizer: None. The paper is a hotspot characterization methodology, not an optimizer. The only design-space exploration is a manual sweep of unit-area scaling (e.g. fpIWin, RATs, RFs at up to 10x) and uniform IC area scaling (pdf pages 9-10).
original_setup.controller: None. No thermal controller or DVFS/throttling policy is simulated. Throttling is discussed only as a motivation, and 1.4 V / 5 GHz is held fixed as a turbo operating point (pdf pages 2-3).
original_setup.benchmark: SPEC2006 single-threaded gobmk, run on each of 7 cores individually after idle warmup (Fig. 9, pdf page 8). The 7nm Skylake-like 7-core client CPU runs a 200M-instruction region of interest with a 1M-cycle time step, at 1.4 V and 5 GHz, with Tth=80 C, MLTDth=25 C and a 1 mm radius.

thermal_observable.location: Maximum localized temperature difference (MLTD) within a 1 mm radius on the 7nm die while single-threaded gobmk runs after idle warmup; highest for cores 0, 2 and 5. The peak value is read from text ('peaks at almost 70 C'), not from a digitized figure, so it is approximate.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Peak over time of the die-wide MLTD (maximum over thermal pixels of the temperature difference to neighbors within 1 mm), reported for the first ~20 ms of the workload; the 14nm part peaks under 60 C.

physical_mismatches.reason: No complete floorplan experiment can be extracted. The paper packet gives no per-block x_m, y_m, width_m, height_m and no per-block power_rows for the gobmk scenario. Only Table I core areas (1.25 mm2 at 7nm) and a Fig. 5 floorplan image are provided. Total chip power is not split into blocks because no rule is published, so the floorplan is empty.

The original uses a multi-layer 3D-ICE stack with an active/bulk silicon split, solder TIM, copper heat spreader, thermal grease and a modeled finned heatsink with fan. A steady-state 2D Studio model with simplified package layers cannot reproduce the transient cooling path and thermal time constants behind the MLTD result.

The observable is transient. MLTD is evaluated over time with a 1M-cycle (~0.2 ms at 5 GHz) step, after a non-uniform idle-warmup thermal initialization. A steady-state solve does not capture this time-dependent behavior or the initial-condition dependence.

The MLTD is computed on a 100 µm thermal grid with a 1 mm radius over a 7-core die including AVX512, SoC/IMC and I/O units. Matching it requires the same resolution and unit set, which are not provided in the packet.

The power comes from a heavily modified McPAT (14/10/7nm scaling with calibrated Cdyn, reported errors of 11-20% on the validation sets) coupled to Sniper, with temperature-dependent leakage. Studio cannot reproduce this performance-power-thermal co-simulation loop.

There is no 3D-IC, interposer, optimizer, controller or reliability model in the original beyond the sigmoid severity metric, so none of these can be compared. Only the thermal stack and solver differ materially.

studio_assumptions: The bundled Studio package/material assumptions were not provided in the packet, so they cannot be stated. Any Studio run would use its own default package stack and material properties, which differ from the 3D-ICE Table II layers and the HS483-ND/fan heatsink.
No claim of exact replication is made, and the GitHub/Zenodo URLs are not treated as proof that the required inputs exist.

methods.note: The method descriptions (3D-ICE v3.0.0, Sniper ROB model, McPAT 1.2, Definition 1, 1 mm radius, 80/25 C thresholds) match pp.3-5. But experiment.kind is custom_2d_steady while the extraction itself says steady_2d_relevant=false and lists essential mismatches: transient, multi-layer stack with heatsink and fan, idle-warmup initial state. A 2D steady reproduction of a transient multi-layer observable is therefore unsupported. The aggregation of the 70 C peak (die-wide max over pixels) is also inferred.

code.note: The assets list is empty. The GitHub and both Zenodo links appear only as paper text (pp.1, 13). Nothing was inspected: no repository files, versions, Sniper/McPAT modifications or 3D-ICE scripts. A bare URL is not evidence.

parameters.note: The Table II conductivities, heat capacities, heights, Table IV Psi/TDP, 1.4 V, 5 GHz, thresholds, 50% area scaling and unit conversions check out against pp.3-5. However, the scenario claims a 5 mm2 die at 14nm scaled to about 1.25 mm2 per core, while Table I lists 5/2.5/1.25 mm2 as core area. The text on p.3 says 'approximately a 5mm2 die'. The extraction notes this ambiguity but still asserts the die-area interpretation in the scenario. No actual die dimensions are given.

config.note: No 3D-ICE stack description file, floorplan file, warmup power trace, initial temperature field, heatsink HTC or geometry, or active/bulk layer split was supplied. The ambient used in the Fig. 9 transient runs is not stated. The 40 C ambient is only for the TDP calculation.

data.note: Fig. 9 (p.8) has no supplied image or digitization; the ~70 C and <60 C values come only from text on p.7. There are no per-block geometries (Fig. 5 is an image only) and no per-block or total gobmk 7nm power for the same scenario. The floorplan list is empty, so the floorplan-block power coverage check cannot be satisfied. No decisive figure was visually verified.

assessment.summary: The feasibility gate returned not_2d_applicable (simulation_allowed=false, comparison_valid=false), so Studio did not run: simulation status is 'skipped'. The selected scenario is HotGauge Fig. 9, a transient perf-power-thermal co-simulation of a 7nm Skylake-like 7-core CPU running single-threaded gobmk after idle warmup. It reports a peak MLTD (1 mm radius) of almost 70 C at 7nm versus under 60 C at 14nm. The extraction proposed a custom_2d_steady experiment with an empty floorplan and no power_w, which failed input validation. It has no transient trace and is not a replication. No Studio-derived temperature or MLTD exists, so no numerical comparison with the ~70 C paper value is made. The paper values (about 70 C and under 60 C at 7nm and 14nm, 80 C and 25 C thresholds) are text-derived and approximate, and are context only. Qualitatively, the paper shows that hotspot severity grows from 14nm to 7nm as power density rises with area scaling, and that the hottest core varies with position. These are the paper's own findings and were not checked against any Studio output. The final verdict is that no result can be assessed or confirmed. The extraction lacks per-block geometry and power, and the evidence items lack valid page or asset locators.
limitations: Studio was not run (skipped by the gate), so there is no simulated output and no replication or numerical comparison of any kind.

Gate failures: custom experiment lacks 1-128 blocks and a power_w object; evidence items 0-35 lack valid page or pinned asset locators; no cited thermal observable or steady/transient regime was accepted; adversarial methods/code/parameters/config/data checks are unresolved; and independent page/asset review is pending.

Regime mismatch: the paper observable is transient MLTD over time (about 0.2 ms steps at 5 GHz, after non-uniform idle warmup), while any custom 2D steady run has no transient trace and cannot capture time constants or initial-condition dependence.

Observable mismatch: the paper's MLTD is a die-wide maximum over a 100 um thermal grid with a 1 mm radius, reported over roughly the first 20 ms. Its exact aggregation is only described qualitatively, and a steady 2D peak or gradient would not match the location or aggregation.

Boundary and stack mismatch: 3D-ICE with an active/bulk silicon split, solder TIM, copper spreader, thermal grease and an HS483-ND heatsink with fan at 6000 rpm, versus Studio's unspecified default package and material assumptions. The effective heat transfer coefficient and the ambient used for the Fig. 9 runs are not stated.
Power mismatch: Sniper plus modified McPAT power with temperature-dependent leakage and 11-20% reported errors is not reproducible in Studio, and no per-block or total gobmk power split is published.
Missing inputs: no numeric floorplan (Fig. 5 is an image; Table I gives only areas, and the 5 mm2 die/core statement is ambiguous), no power rows, no digitized Fig. 9 data, and no idle-warmup trace.
The GitHub and Zenodo links are unpinned, absent from the packet, and unverified, so they do not demonstrate that the required inputs exist.

The approximately 70 C and under 60 C values come from text (one being an upper bound) and not from digitized data. They are temperature differences, not absolute temperatures, and per-core values are only qualitative.
